characters.name: Gladias
characters.voice_notes: Protagonist of the Veridia chapters. Thoughtful, calm, gentle, philosophical, with an occasional mischievous streak; a little awkward under pressure. Acolyte of the Order of Steering (accepted as a Keeper in ch. 8). Husband of Seila, father of Zven and Lily. Many of his lines are subvocalised whispers through a neck band.

characters.name: Mov
characters.age: adult (established Order member; Gladias's peer or slightly senior)
characters.voice_notes: Gladias's close friend and mentor in the Order of Steering (a Keeper, selected as a Herald in ch. 8). Wry, sarcastic, sharp, security-paranoid but warm underneath; talks fast and knowledgeably. Partly heard by call/earpiece.

characters.name: first man on bench
characters.voice_notes: Passer-by chatting on a bench outside Greater Plum Harbor; has been inside, relaxed and worldly.

characters.name: second man on bench
characters.voice_notes: His companion on the bench; never been inside Greater Plum Harbor, sympathetic to it, exasperated and a bit ranting.

characters.name: Emerald
characters.voice_notes: Gladias's local AI assistant running on his hand device, heard in his ear; neutral, concise, informative.

characters.name: Delwart
characters.voice_notes: The mysterious anonymous messenger from ch. 1. Smooth, self-assured, persuasive, slightly showy and quietly menacing; an ideologue who wants the Steering system abolished and recruits Keepers.

characters.name: entrance gate machine
characters.voice_notes: Short synthetic confirmation voice from a credential-checking gate; robotic but approving. Ch. 1 is the concert gate, ch. 3 the Greater Plum Harbor gate; same type of voice.

notes: M is Mov throughout the tunnel scene; the only other M is the Greater Plum Harbor gate machine at 3:76. B and V are the two men on the bench (the letters do not obviously match their labels; attribution follows the speech tags and turn-taking: B = 3:62, 3:64, 3:72; V = 3:63, 3:66, 3:71). E (3:69) is Emerald, Gladias's AI; 3:67 is Gladias's silent subvocalised question to it. The propaganda poster at 3:7 is narrator-read written text signed by Lord Ephelion, who speaks in ch. 8. 3:9 is Gladias's thought inside narration.
